statement: A flag shape is rotated a quarter turn clockwise about its bottom-left corner. Which of the descriptions matches the result?

figure.alt: A flag shape drawn as an upright pole with a small triangle attached to the top right of the pole, standing on a marked corner point at the bottom of the pole.

choices.text: the pole points right and the triangle is below it
the pole points right and the triangle is above it
choices.misconception: I turned the pole the right way but kept the triangle on the side it started on.

choices.text: the pole points left and the triangle is above it
choices.misconception: I turned the shape anticlockwise instead of clockwise.

choices.text: the pole points down and the triangle is to the left
choices.misconception: I turned the shape half a turn instead of a quarter turn.

choices.text: the pole points up and the triangle is on the left
choices.misconception: I reflected the shape in a vertical line instead of rotating it.

hints: Turn the page, do not imagine it.
A quarter turn clockwise sends up to the right. Track the pole first, then ask which side of the pole the triangle ends up on - it travels with the pole, it does not stay put.
Up becomes right, so the pole points right. The triangle was on the right of an upward pole, and turning clockwise carries it to below a rightward pole.

solutions.reliable: Track one part at a time. A quarter turn clockwise sends the direction up to the direction right, so the upright pole ends up pointing right. The triangle sat on the right-hand side of the upward pole; clockwise, right becomes down, so the triangle ends up below the rightward pole. The transferable idea: rotate each feature by the same rule rather than picturing the whole shape at once.

whyOnTest: Rotation questions are answered wrongly when a student turns the main feature but leaves the details where they were.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
